title: Reader shapes - the framework-facing schema of the demand-side inputs
contract: The framework's demand and measurement readers consume three families of jurisdiction-published data: census attributes, household-travel-survey aggregates, and classified traffic counts. Each jurisdiction publishes them in its own vocabulary (ABS G-table column names, NSW HTS labels, RMS period labels). This document declares the shape the FRAMEWORK reads - the fields and vocabulary its own code depends on - and each city supplies a thin adapter at cities/<city>/extract/reader_shapes.py that maps its published shapes to this schema AT READ TIME. The framework resolves the adapter through src/city.py (city.readers()), the only module that knows where a city lives; no artefact is rewritten and raw downloads stay immutable.
adapter_location: cities/<city>/extract/reader_shapes.py, resolved by city.readers(). A city without one cannot run the readers listed under each family's consumed_by.

adapter_functions.mode_share_table(): Returns one row per (area_name, mode_category) for the base-year survey vintage at the survey's target-geography level, as a list of dicts with the columns below.
adapter_functions.mode_category_labels(): framework mode_category -> the label the city's survey (and its derived validation targets) print for it. Used to match target rows, which carry the survey's own wording.
adapter_functions.survey_vintage(): The survey-vintage label of the base year, exactly as the city's published files and validation targets spell it (e.g. a financial year).

columns.area_name: the survey area's name, matching city.json mode_share_target.filter_value for the target geography
columns.mode_category: one of the framework categories below
columns.trips: unlinked trip count for the category in this area (weighting quantity; null where the survey publishes shares only)
columns.linked_share_pct: the published LINKED main-mode share, percent (null where only trips are published)

hts_mode_share.note: The linked/unlinked distinction is load-bearing: a MATSim main-mode share is the linked concept (DECISIONS.md 12.1). walk_linked is the walk stage of a PT journey and is 0.0 by construction in a linked share.
hts_readers_still_source_shaped: src/build/build_activity_chains.py (hts_purpose.csv and hts_mode.csv with NSW labels, FINANCIAL_YEAR selection)

adapter_functions.total_volume_counts(): Returns the total-vehicle-volume count observations - the rows whose classification means ALL vehicles (however the agency spells that) - as a pandas DataFrame with exactly the columns below, one row per published observation (no adapter-side aggregation).

columns.period: one of: weekday, weekend - normalised from the agency's period vocabulary
columns.volume: mean daily traffic count for the period

classified_counts.note: Only the fields the framework reads are declared. Heavy-vehicle classes are consumed by city-owned measurement (the freight profile adapter), not by the framework.

census_attributes.status: DECLARED, ADAPTER PENDING - these readers remain source-shaped
consumed_by_still_source_shaped: src/build/build_population.py (ABS G01/G04A+B/G15/G17A+B/G34/G35/G36/G43/G46A+B/G60A+B column names, age-band spellings and sex-split table pairs)
src/build/build_zone_attractions.py (ABS G01/G36 and W09A+B place-of-work tables)

per_residence_zone: population by single-year age and sex (grouped bands accepted at the distribution tail)
labour force status conditional on age band and sex (employed FT/PT, unemployed, not in labour force)
full-time share of adult education attendees
share of employed persons who travelled to work on census day (sweep lower bound only)
per_workplace_zone: jobs by industry division at place of work

census_attributes.reason_left: The population synthesiser consumes the ABS tables' own banding, dual column spellings and sex-split table pairs at ~40 read sites; normalising them is a data-pipeline rebuild, not a read-time mapping, and is deliberately NOT done in the same change that adapts the two thin families (issue #62 A5). The declared field list above is the target shape for that rebuild.
